answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with mutual-guarantee cohorts: a newcomer joins only when existing members stake collateral for it, like nectar shared only with trusted visitors to a haven. If the newcomer fakes work or double-votes, the sponsors' stake is slashed too, so honest agents vet newcomers carefully. An attacker must bribe honest sponsors or fund a whole fake cohort, and a cohort grown in the dark, like water carving karst caves, still has capped weight until it passes repeated audits, so every fake identity puts real collateral at risk.
